title: 1981-04-16_Pat_128.txt
concise_summary: PKD articulates a Protestant existentialist theology of salvation grounded in human moral choice and radical dependence on God, arguing that knowledge and moral freedom must remain bipolarized for Christ's redemptive return to remain hidden yet eternally effective. This system derives from his solution to the riddle of 'Tears' and positions man's cry to God (not God's grace imposed) as the initiating act, with justification occurring through the Holy Spirit in a singular moment of ontological crisis akin to Heidegger's existential decision.
key_claims: True moral choice can only occur when the person does not know the truth, because knowledge of consequences would eliminate free will and reduce ethics to pragmatic reward-seeking
Christ's return in glory is a 'disclose' (mystical disclosure) rather than a historical event that failed; the apparent failure of Christianity serves as a top-level agency in the system itself
Salvation is initiated by man's absolute cry to God for help (the Paraclete), based on recognition of his total powerlessness, not by God's prior grace; man must act first
Faith (pistis) is an existential act of turning to God, expressing utter dependence and trust, not mere intellectual belief; God responds only after man chooses
The concept 'fate' (heimarmene) must be reconceived as 'providentia'—the absolute power of God as Pantocrator—before causal freedom from the world is even conceptually possible
recurring_concepts: The secrecy theme / steganographia—why divine truth must be veiled to preserve moral choice
Bipolarization of knowledge and freedom—the paradox that truth-knowledge destroys the freedom necessary for genuine morality
Ontological crisis / existential decision—drawing on Heidegger, the singular moment when person recognizes total dependence on God
Justification—the Protestant doctrine of God's response to man's cry, granting rightness to his being through the Holy Spirit
Pantocrator—God as absolute power and guarantor of being; contrasted with heimarmene (fate as world-causality)
Paraclete—the Holy Spirit summoned by man's call for help; the mode of divine response to human moral action
The riddle of 'Tears'—PKD's solution to understanding Acts as 'Gospel of the Holy Spirit' and Protestant Pauline doctrine
Holy Spirit authorship—the doctrine that the Holy Spirit, not human authors, is the true author of scriptural/revelatory material
people_entities: Philip K. Dick (author, developing his salvation theology)
Jesus / Christ—central to doctrine of return, self-sacrifice, ethics
Paul / St. Paul—Pauline doctrine of salvation through faith; contrast to Catholic grace theology

Paul Tillich—20th-century existential Protestant theologian congruent with PKD's position
Martin Heidegger—existential philosophy of ontological crisis and authentic decision
Joachim of Fiore—medieval theology of three status; PKD suggests 'Tears' may relate to Joachim's third age

texts_works: Acts (New Testament)—'Gospel of the Holy Spirit'; subject of the riddle of 'Tears'
Romans (New Testament, implicit)—Paul's doctrine of justification by faith

VALIS (PKD's own novel)—his revelation that others disbelieve despite or because of knowledge

autobiographical: PKD wrote a letter to Isa in which he defined salvation as recognition of absolute dependence on God and utter faith
He did not realize, when writing the letter, that he was reaffirming Pauline doctrine of salvation through faith
He has solved the riddle posed in 'Tears,' which led him to this theology of secret and bipolarized knowledge
His revelation in VALIS is one he expects others will disbelieve, which he now understands is necessary to the system
theological_motifs: Salvation by faith (not works)—Protestant Pauline soteriology
Justification—God's act of declaring man righteous through the Holy Spirit; occurs once, at ontological crisis
Grace (heterodox reversal)—God grants grace after man takes the first step (calls out), not before
The Holy Spirit—indispensable agent of justification and divine response; Protestant emphasis contra Catholic theology
Total depravity / radical powerlessness—man's ontological worthlessness; cannot save himself
Ontological dependence on God—man's being is wholly derived from God's being; without God, man will cease to exist
Absolute faith / pistis—not intellectual belief but existential act of turning and trusting
Divine hiddenness / apophatic theology—truth must remain hidden for moral choice to remain free
Paraclete / Holy Spirit—summoned by man's cry for help; divine responder to human initiative
literary_self_ref: VALIS (his own novel)—the revelation whose truth the AI voice spoke of, yet which people disbelieve; now PKD understands why disbelief is necessary
'Tears' (his work or cipher)—the riddle whose solution undergirds his entire theological system; source of the Pauline/Holy Spirit reading of Acts
symbols_images: Steganographia / veiling—the necessary obscuring of truth to preserve moral freedom
The cry / call to God—the concrete image of man's existential act, man reaching out for the Paraclete
Fate (heimarmene) transformed to providentia—conceptual conversion from world-power to God-power; the mind's transformation before justification occurs
God as absolute friend and protector—God the father completing his creative work through justification
The final act of justification—God's response completing the original creation of man
Man and God reunited—with man seeking God and God seeking man; reconciliation through mutual orientation
tensions: PKD asserts man must take the first step (calling on God), which contradicts orthodox Catholic and Protestant views of grace as prior. He recognizes this as 'heterodox' and 'radical' yet defends it as grounded in existential choice.

He claims moral knowledge and freedom are 'bipolarized'—mutually exclusive—yet argues that God is in 'absolute control' using disbelief as an instrument. The resolution is that true control works through human ignorance and choice.

PKD expected his VALIS revelation to convince others through knowledge, but now realizes knowledge is precisely what prevents conversion. He calls this his 'error' yet it reveals the system's necessity.

The apparent non-fulfillment of Christ's return in glory is described both as a 'fiction that has to obtain' and as 'always + eternally in fact fulfilled'—a paradox between phenomenal history and noumenal reality.

He describes faith as grounded in 'Pauline insight + position' yet acknowledges his position is 'heterodox' and 'more radical' than Luther or Calvin, departing from the Reformation on the question of which party (God or man) initiates.
evidence_quotes: Thus the 'secrecy theme' is simply unavoidable. there just plain is no other way that it can be done... the veiling, is essential to the situation to a degele that by the very essence of logic admits of no mitigation or compromise.
the real issue is moral (viz: and it is in Judaism, the parent of Xtianity. most clearly + fully in the domain of morality that God's presence is found + disclosed).

paradoxically, the freedom o true moral choice can + does only occur when the person does not know the truth (actual situation, which is to say real consequences). Thus for inevitable reasons, moral choice + knowledge are bipolarized.

My error is to reason: (1) knowledge of the truth. (2) Then as a result, right conduct but (2) would have ceased to be based on free choice, true ethical decision + would be merely the act would be done for tangible smart reward, + this has nothing to do with morality

what is perhaps unusual - heterodox in my position is that I assert that man not God, must take the first step; it is God who responds to man, not man to God... but this only reveals my position as thoroughly existential; salvation hinges on a human decision + act based on that decision
uncertainty_flags: The exact nature of 'Tears' is unclear—whether it is a text PKD has read, a cipher he is decoding, or his own work. The riddle's content is not specified in this segment.
PKD mentions an 'Isa' letter but provides no date, context, or whether Isa is a real person or fictional. The letter's full contents are not quoted.
'St. Sophia's approaching—or fulfilled—return' is mentioned as spoken by the AI voice, but her identity and what 'return' signifies remains opaque.
The phrase 'meta-abstraction' appears without definition near the end; unclear what object or concept PKD is referring to.
PKD states his views derive from 'solving the riddle of Tears' but does not explain the riddle or its solution in this entry.
Joachim's 'third status' is alluded to as related to 'Tears' but the connection is asserted without explanation.
reading_excerpt: what is perhaps unusual - heterodox in my position is that I assert that man not God, must take the first step; it is God who responds to man, not man to God, + this runs counter to the whole orthodox view of grace both Catholic + protestant. but this only reveals my position as thoroughly existential; salvation hinges on a human decision + act based on that decision, God will not respond unless the person chooses, + he chooses entirely of his own free will.
